records.segregation: In trans in the affected subjects; segregated with the myopathy in all six family members
quotes: We ascertained a non-consanguineous Caucasian family of mixed European ancestry in which three of four siblings had an undiagnosed autosomal recessive myopathy, which resembled MmD in some respects

All three patients had childhood onset scoliosis and were treated with spinal fusion surgery, and beginning at age 10–11 years, they all developed respiratory problems treated with bilevel positive airway pressure ventilation at night.

the heterozygous missense mutations c.976T > C (p.C326R) and c.2320T > C (p.C774R) in MEGF10, the sole remaining candidate, were confirmed by Sanger sequencing to be in trans in affected subjects and to segregate with the myopathy in all six family members.

records.segregation: Heterozygous in an unaffected parent; no second mutation was found
quotes: Subject 105-1 was a female Caucasian with distant Portuguese ancestry, diagnosed with MmD. No one else in her family was affected. At several weeks of age, she presented with hypotonia, initially manifesting as a weak neck and floppy head.
A markedly high arched palate and failure to thrive as a result of poor feeding were noted, as were blue-tinged sclera and hyperflexible joints.
The c.211C > T mutation was heterozygous in an unaffected parent of subject 105-1, so it was not de novo dominant.

quotes: We undertook exome sequencing in a 66 year old male with a 20 year history of progressive proximal and distal weakness of upper and lower limbs, facial weakness and dysphagia, who developed respiratory failure requiring ventilation while still ambulant in his 50s.
Muscle biopsy demonstrated myopathic changes with aggregation of myofibrillar proteins.
Mutations in MEGF10 were identified: a novel essential splice site (c.1426+1G>T) and a novel missense variant (c.352T>C, p.(Cys118Arg)).

quotes: This patient is a 22-year-old boy, born to healthy consanguineous parents without family history of neuromuscular diseases.
Exome sequencing led to the identification of the homozygous variant (NM_001256545.2): c.2096G > C (p.Cys699Ser) in the MEGF10 gene.
Sanger sequencing was also performed and confirmed that the patient was homozygous for the variant, and both parents were carriers.

notes.statement: Croci et al. (2022) noted that although their patient carried a homozygous missense variant affecting a cysteine in an EGF-like domain, he had early-onset myopathy with a progressive course. They suggested a continuum between classic EMARDD and mvEMARDD rather than two separate forms.
quotes: Although our patient carried a missense variant, he displayed an early-onset myopathy with progressive course.

our report proposes a continuum in the phenotypes associated with MEGF10 variants, which include a clinical and histopathological progression of the disease and represent a novelty from the dichotomy between the early onset classic severe EMARDD and mvEMARDD

notes.statement: Croci et al. (2022) found nonspecific changes in their patient's first muscle biopsy and myofibrillar changes with minicores in a later biopsy. They proposed that minicores, which mark the later-onset group, may result from a long-standing myofibrillar disease process that starts in infancy.
quotes: Thus, we propose that minicores that mark the late onset group, can actually be a consequence of a longstanding myofibrillar pathological processes starting in infancy.

notes.statement: Croci et al. (2022) suggested testing the MEGF10 gene in patients with suspected myofibrillar myopathy who have childhood-onset progressive myopathy, scoliosis, contractures, and respiratory involvement.
quotes: MEGF10 gene should be tested in suspected MFM patients with childhood onset of progressive myopathy, scoliosis and retraction, and respiratory defect

notes.statement: In a review of all 20 reported MEGF10 cases, Harris et al. (2018) confirmed a genotype-phenotype correlation: patients with at least 1 null mutation had onset of respiratory dysfunction in the first year of life, whereas those with 2 missense mutations had respiratory dysfunction at 10 years of age or much later.
quotes: We performed a detailed review of all reported MEGF10 cases (n = 20), and confirmed the presence of a genotype-phenotype correlation, namely that with ≥1 null mutation onset of respiratory dysfunction occurs in the first year of life, whereas with 2 missense mutations, respiratory dysfunction occurs at 10 years old or much later

notes.statement: Harris et al. (2018) concluded that their findings expanded the phenotype of MEGF10 mutations to include onset in the fifth decade.
quotes: Our findings expand the phenotype of MEGF10 mutations to include onset in the 5th decade, and discuss the spectrum of MEGF10 related disease.

notes.statement: Takayama et al. (2016) noted that cysteine mutations in the extracellular EGF-like domain of MEGF10 may be responsible for the milder phenotype; their finding of a homozygous frameshift in a patient with EMARDD and a compound heterozygous genotype including the novel p.Cys810Tyr missense in a patient with the milder phenotype was taken to indicate a genotype-phenotype correlation in MEGF10 myopathy.
quotes: Cysteine mutations in the extracellular EGF-like domain may be responsible for the milder phenotype, but the relationship is not conclusive because of the few reports of this disorder.
This is the first report on East Asian patients with MEGF10 myopathy showing two phenotypes, indicating the genotype-phenotype correlation in MEGF10 myopathy.

notes.statement: Boyden et al. (2012) carried out genomewide linkage analysis in family 1030 under a recessive model and found positive LOD scores at 16 loci. MEGF10 lay within a linkage peak on chromosome 5 that reached the maximum possible LOD score of 1.329.
quotes: Family 1030 produced positive LOD scores at sixteen genomic loci, ten of which approached the theoretical maximum LOD score of 1.329
MEGF10 lies within a linkage peak on chromosome 5 that reached the maximum possible LOD score of 1.329.

notes.statement: Boyden et al. (2012) screened the entire MEGF10 open reading frame in 190 patients with unexplained myopathies and selected exons in another 82. They found only one patient with a heterozygous mutation, p.R71W. The 2 family 1030 mutations were absent from 715 and 645 control subjects, respectively, and both affected cysteine residues were conserved in all 43 species examined.
quotes: By Sanger sequencing, we screened the entire open reading frame of MEGF10 in 190 additional patients with unexplained myopathies, as well as selected exons in another 82 patients.

The c.976T > C and c.2320T > C mutations were also absent from 715 and 645 genotyped unaffected control subjects, respectively (Table 1). The p.C326 and p.C774 positions are both completely conserved in 43 species.

notes.statement: Boyden et al. (2012) noted that the phenotype in their patients with missense mutations was milder than that previously reported in patients with MEGF10 nonsense and frameshift mutations. Minicores were prominent in their patients but had not been noted in the families with null mutations. They suggested that residual MEGF10 function might explain the milder phenotype, though genetic background or other factors could also contribute.
quotes: The phenotypes described therein are generally similar to those of families 1030 and 105, but are more severe.

Accordingly, affected members of family 1030 may retain a small amount of residual MEGF10 function, though genetic background or other factors could also account for clinical heterogeneity between families.
Moreover, minicores were not noted in the biopsies from the reported families with null mutations but were a prominent feature in our patients with missense mutations.

notes.statement: Boyden et al. (2012) knocked down megf10 in zebrafish with 4 splice-blocking morpholinos. The morphants had curled or bent tails, impaired swimming, unhatched eggs, disorganized somites and reduced birefringence. Immunostaining and electron microscopy showed gaps between myofibers and myofibrillar disorganization, consistent with a myopathic process.
quotes: Anti-megf10 morpholinos resulted in several phenotypes at 4 days post-fertilization, generally including curled or bent tails, impaired swimming behavior, and diminished motility in response to touch, all consistent with a myopathy

MO2-treated zebrafish muscle showed widespread myofibrillar disorganization and decreased striation (Online Resource 15). These structural defects suggest that the motor impairments of morphant fish were due at least in part to a myopathic process, as opposed to a neuropathy.

notes.statement: Boyden et al. (2012) noted that the p.C326R and p.C774R mutations replace conserved cysteines in atypical EGF-like domains and likely disrupt disulfide bonds. They hypothesized that the resulting loss of MEGF10 function could cause excessive differentiation of satellite cells, depleting the self-renewing cells needed for muscle regeneration.
quotes: The p.C326R and p.C774R mutations substitute the fourth and sixth cysteines of EGF-like domains six and sixteen, respectively, for arginines.

the p.C326R and p.C774R mutations in family 1030 likely result in a loss of MEGF10 function, in which case we hypothesize that excessive differentiation of satellite cells could deplete the population of self-renewing cells available to regenerate damaged muscle fibers.

notes.statement: Holterman et al. (2007) found that Megf10, the mouse homolog of human MEGF10, was expressed in quiescent satellite cells of adult mouse skeletal muscle and in proliferating myoblasts, but not in differentiated myofibers. Expression was high in brain and in regenerating muscle, and it rose more than 100-fold when satellite cells were activated.
quotes: We identify here the multiple epidermal growth factor repeat transmembrane protein Megf10 as a quiescent satellite cell marker that is also expressed in skeletal myoblasts but not in differentiated myofibers.
high levels of Megf10 expression were detected in the brain and in regenerating skeletal muscle 3 d after cardiotoxin injection
Megf10 expression was up-regulated over 100-fold in activated satellite cells (Fig. 1 C).

notes.statement: Holterman et al. (2007) found that retroviral overexpression of Megf10 in C2C12 myoblasts increased proliferation and inhibited differentiation and fusion. The infected cells entered a reversible quiescent state rather than terminally differentiating. Overexpression also lowered MyoD and Pax7 protein levels and raised Myf5 levels.
quotes: Retroviral expression of Megf10 in myoblasts results in enhanced proliferation and inhibited differentiation. Infected myoblasts that fail to differentiate undergo cell cycle arrest and can reenter the cell cycle upon serum restimulation.
C2C12 cells overexpressing Megf10 showed a dramatic down-regulation of MyoD and Pax7 proteins (Fig. 6 A).

notes.statement: Holterman et al. (2007) found that siRNA knockdown of Megf10 in activated satellite cells on isolated mouse myofibers reduced cell numbers through myogenin activation and precocious differentiation, and depleted the self-renewing Pax7+/MyoD- population. Knockdown in MyoD-null myoblasts lowered expression of Notch1, Notch2, Notch3 and Hes1. The authors concluded that Megf10 impinges on Notch signaling to regulate the balance between satellite cell proliferation and differentiation.
quotes: Megf10 silencing in activated satellite cells on individual fibers or in cultured myoblasts results in a dramatic reduction in the cell number, caused by myogenin activation and precocious differentiation as well as a depletion of the self-renewing Pax7+/MyoD- population.

Notably, we observed down-regulation of Notch receptors Notch 1 (0.56-fold; P = 0.001), Notch 2 (0.64-fold; P = 0.027), and Notch 3 (0.41-fold; P = 0.018), as well as down-regulation of Notch downstream effector Hes 1 (0.52-fold; P = 0.046) after Megf10 knockdown.
We conclude that Megf10 represents a novel transmembrane protein that impinges on Notch signaling to regulate the satellite cell population balance between proliferation and differentiation.

notes.statement: Holterman et al. (2007) cloned full-length mouse Megf10, which shares more than 94% amino acid identity with human MEGF10 and resembles the probable orthologs CED-1 (C. elegans) and Draper (Drosophila). When expressed from a retrovirus, Megf10 localized to the plasma membrane and the cytoplasm.
quotes: revealing MDp67 to be the mouse homologue of human MEGF10 with >94% identity at the amino acid level. These two sequences are also similar to probable orthologues CED-1 (Caenorhabditis elegans) and Draper (Drosophila melanogaster
Western analysis of the fractions demonstrated that retrovirally expressed Megf10 localized to the plasma membrane, as well as to the cytoplasm of infected cells (Fig. 3 A).
